title: The City of Las Cruces' Comments on El Paso Electric Company's Proposed Second Notice to EPE Customers and Social Media Campaign [Comment]

documents.name: DOC-000465751-26
documents.text:
BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF EL PASO                         )
ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR REVISION OF ITS RETAIL                         )   Docket No. 25-00082-UT
ELECTRIC RATES PURSUANT TO ADVICE NOTICE                            )
NO. 317                                                             )

               THE CITY OF LAS CRUCES’ COMMENTS ON
               EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY’S PROPOSED
     SECOND NOTICE TO EPE CUSTOMERS AND SOCIAL MEDIA CAMPAIGN

       COMES NOW the City of Las Cruces (the “City” or “CLC”), by and through the

undersigned attorneys, and pursuant to Paragraph E of the Order Establishing Revised Procedural

Schedule and Addressing Outstanding Motions (“Revised Procedural Order”) issued on August

27, 2026, submits its comments on El Paso Electric Company’s (“EPE” or “Company”) proposed

form of website notice to EPE customers, filed on September 3, 2026. These comments reiterate

to a substantial degree the positions asserted by the City, Doña Ana County, and pro se intervenors

Stephen Fischmann and Philip B. Simpson in the Joint Motion for Clarification and

Reconsideration of Order Establishing Revised Procedural Schedule and Order Extending

Suspension Period for Advice Notice No. 317, filed on September 8, 2026 (“Joint Motion”), but

also elaborate on those concerns.

       First, the City will comment upon the Company’s (Proposed) Second Notice to EPE

Customers, filed on September 3, 2026, as part of EPE’s Notice of Compliance Filing of Proposed

Form of Website Notice (“Notice of Compliance Filing”).

       Second, the City will comment upon the minimal amount of information that the Notice of

Compliance Filing provides about EPE’s proposed social media campaign, which information is

contained in the (Proposed) Second Notice to EPE Customers itself rather than in an explanatory

pleading to the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission (“Commission” or “NMPRC”).
 I.      THE (PROPOSED) SECOND NOTICE TO EPE CUSTOMERS

        1.     The (Proposed) Second Notice to EPE Customers is contradictory and confusing.

The first paragraph on the first page of the proposed notice states that “the non-fuel base rate

revenue deficiency shown in EPE’s proposed cost of service changed from $70.6 to $70.7 million

and now demonstrates the need for a 50.5% base rate increase.” See Notice of Compliance Filing

at (Proposed) Second Notice to EPE Customers p.1 of 6 (unnumbered). The second paragraph on

the same page then states that “EPE’s previously noticed revised rates, set forth in Advice Notice

No. 317, represent the maximum rates that can be approved in this proceeding.” See id.

        2.     The (Proposed) Form of Notice to EPE Customers does not inform customers of

anything about the previously noticed revised rates other than that they are set forth in Advice

Notice No. 317. See id.; see also id., passim. One would not expect that an EPE customer

reviewing this public notice would understand what “Advice Notice No. 317” is, let alone where

to find it.

        3.     Nor would one expect an EPE customer to grasp the convolutions of this Docket

No. 25-00082-UT and appreciate, based on EPE’s references to the July 16, 2026, order requiring

EPE to file an Amended Notice and to “EPE’s previously noticed revised rates, set forth in Advice

Notice No. 317,” that EPE’s original application to amend its New Mexico retail base rates has

been pending since March 27, 2026, and that notice of that application was previously emailed to

New Mexico customers who receive their bills electronically, mailed as bill stuffers to New

Mexico customers who receive their bills in the mail, published in the Las Cruces Sun-News,

posted on the Company’s website, and advertised on social media, as well as posted on the

NMPRC’s website. See id. at p.1 of 6 (unnumbered); see also Declaration of Michelle A. Pedroza

in Support of EPE’s Proof of Notice to Customers (June 5, 2026); https://www.prc.nm.gov/wp-

content/uploads/2026/04/25-00082-Attachment-A-Notice-Final.pdf (accessed on Sept. 4, 2026).

                                                2
        4.      The (Proposed) Form of Notice states, incorrectly, that “Listed below is a

comparison of present and proposed rates for the Residential customer class under Advice Notice

No. 317 proposed by EPE.” See Notice of Compliance Filing at (Proposed) Second Notice to EPE

Customers p.3 of 6 (unnumbered). Under that assert are listed the standard Residential Rate No.

1 current and proposed Phase 1 and Phase 2 rates that are proposed in EPE’s Amended Application,

but which are not the rates proposed in Advice Notice No. 317. Compare id. & Amended

Application, [Amended] Direct Testimony of George Novela at Ex. GN-4 (Aug. 6, 2026) with

Docket No. 26-0000062, EPE’s Advice Notice No. 317 (Mar. 27, 2026).

       5.      Furthermore, the (Proposed) Second Notice to EPE Customers identifies the docket

number for this proceeding only once, on the third page of the proposed form of notice, and does

not identify Docket No. 26-000062, in which Advice Notice No. 317 is on file, anywhere. See

Notice of Compliance Filing at (Proposed) Second Notice to EPE Customers p.3 of 6

(unnumbered) & passim.

       6.      As noted in the Joint Motion, EPE’s (Proposed) Second Notice to EPE Customers

contains a QR code that leads to the original Notice to EPE Customers that was posted on the

Commission’s website concerning the Company’s proposed rates in this case. See Joint Motion

¶ 77; see also supra ¶ 3. While the Commission presumably will update or supplement the notice

on its website once the Hearing Examiners rule on this matter, the City reiterates that the

Commission’s version of notice includes detailed information about current and proposed rate

components for all classes of service that EPE provides in New Mexico, while the (Proposed)

Second Notice to EPE Customers provides just a few figures for Standard Residential Service

under Rate No. 1. See Joint Motion ¶ 78; see also id. at ¶ 77.

       7.      If EPE is now proposing different rates for all classes of service under its Amended

Application, as its testimony, exhibits, schedules, and workpapers now indicate, the Second Notice

                                                3
 to Customers to be posted on both the Commission’s website and the Company’s website should

include all of that information. There is no additional expense for providing critical information

to all of EPE’s New Mexico retail customers electronically, not only to residential customers who

receive service under the standard Rate No. 1 option.

       8.      Moreover, the Commission should take the opportunity to improve the (Proposed)

Second Notice to EPE Ratepayers, as well as the original notices as posted differently on EPE’s

website and the Commission’s website, to make two aspects of the notice more prominent. First,

the docket number (or numbers) of this proceeding should be identified earlier, more often, and in

bold face type. Second, the deadline for motions to intervene and the procedures for filing such

motions should be accentuated. See Joint Motion ¶ 79. The City understands that the primary

reason for giving public notice of EPE’s Amended Application is to provide customers notice of

their revived opportunity to participate formally in this proceeding. The information that they need

should not be buried in the text in two places in the notice. Cf. Notice of Compliance Filing at

(Proposed) Second Notice to EPE Customers p. 4 (unnumbered) (intervention deadline); id. at p.5

(unnumbered) (“To Become a Party”).

II.    THE PROPOSED SOCIAL MEDIA CAMPAIGN

       9.      The Revised Procedural Order directed that EPE’s September 3, 2026, filing “shall

describe the manner in which EPE will conduct a social media campaign for that notice, including

a description of how the social media campaign will connect customers to the form of notice that

will be made available on EPE’s website. ” Revised Procedural Order ¶ E.

       10.     The only description or information provided by EPE is to be found within the

Proposed) Second Notice to EPE Customers itself. See Notice of Compliance Filing at (Proposed)

Second Notice to EPE Customers pp.3-4 of 6 (unnumbered). That text reads:



                                                 4
        El Paso Electric Company ("EPE") intends to conduct a paid social media
       notification campaign related to the Application on Meta platforms, Facebook
       and Instagram, beginning September 15, 2026, for an anticipated duration of
       approximately one week.

       The campaign will be geographically targeted to customers residing within
       EPE's New Mexico service territory through ZIP code-based audience
       selection. In addition, the campaign will utilize relevant professional and
       interest-based targeting criteria, including government agencies and
       individuals with interests related to energy and utility services.

       The advertisement will provide a direct link to the Amended Application Notice
       posted on EPE's website, facilitating customer access to and review of the
       notice.

       11.     EPE’s Notice of Compliance Filing does not explain why the Company chose to

include this minimal, and somewhat irrelevant, information within the text of the (Proposed)

Second Notice to Customers. See Notice of Compliance Filing, passim. Obviously, a separate

statement would have facilitated a more expansion description of the social media campaign.

       12. EPE’s (Proposed) Second Notice to Customers does not describe the text and/or audio

and/or visual content and appearance of the “advertisement” that will provide a link to EPE’s

website. See id. EPE does not describe the duration of the social media “advertisement.” See

Notice of Compliance Filing at (Proposed) Second Notice to EPE Customers.

       13.     EPE does not state how many times this undisclosed advertisement will be

disseminated on each form of social media, the times of day or days of the week in which it will

run, any other advertising or other content with which it may be associated, or any efforts that the

Company will make to assess the effectiveness of its social media advertising. See id.

       14.     EPE does not describe how the advertisement will provide a direct link to the

Amended Application Notice on the Company’s website; merely referring to the epelectric.com

website will not be useful to New Mexico customers. See id.



                                                 5
         15.     EPE does not describe what measures, if any, it will take to assure that its own retail

customers in New Mexico will be reached, other than by using local zip codes in the social media

campaign. See id.

        16.     Importantly, EPE does not explain why it plans to run this social media campaign

for only one week beginning on September 15, 2026, i.e., immediately following the

Commission’s confirmation of the form of notice and the social media campaign. The procedural

schedule provides a full month, until October 16, 2026, for motions to intervene to be filed. See

id.; see also Revised Procedural Order ¶ H.

        17.     EPE’s failure to include specific information about the “advertisement” it will

disseminate through social media and more detailed information about its social media campaign

for directing interested parties to the proposed website notice makes it difficult for parties to file

substantial and thoughtful comments on “EPE’s filed plan for its social media campaign” on or

before September 10, 2026, as the Revised Procedural Order provides. Revised Procedural Order

¶ F; see also id. ¶ E.

        18.     Likewise, EPE’s failure to include specific and detailed information about how it

will conduct a social media campaign for the proposed website notice makes it nearly impossible

for the Hearing Examiners to “issue an Order confirming and/or defining the final form of website

notice, and social media campaign, on or before September 15, 2026.” Id. ¶ G (emphasis in

original). As far as the social media campaign goes, EPE seems to be asking for total discretion

to use an advertisement that it has not revealed to the Commission and the parties in a manner that

it barely outlines.

        19.     EPE’s minimally outlined social media notice plan effectively shifts to the Hearing

Examiners the task of “defining the final . . . social media campaign,”, in a matter of days. See

Revised Procedural Order ¶ G. Whether they can do so in the few days that they have allotted

                                                  6
 under the Revised Procedural Order remains to be seen, but it appears that Staff and the intervenors

will remain in the dark forever.

       20.     The City believes that even before the Hearing Examiners will rule upon the Joint

Motion, the Company’s (Proposed) Second Notice to EPE Customer necessitates a determination

by the Commission on whether the Amended Application is seeking to revise rates in accordance

with the testimony, exhibits, schedules, and workpapers set forth therein, or whether the Company

is seeking approval of the revised rates set forth in Advice Notice No. 317, which was filed in

Docket No. 26-0000062 and was referenced throughout EPE’s original Application. In conjunction

with such a determination, it may be necessary, and it certainly would be helpful, for the

Commission to clarify whether EPE’s original Application, including the errata notices to that

appIication, are to be deemed never to have existed.

       21.     Such determination should be made because issuing ambiguous, confusing, and

even erroneous public notice is not consistent with the public interest or the Public Utility Act.

       WHEREFORE, the City respectfully asks the Commission to take into consideration the

comments set out above and in the Joint Motion filed on September 8, 2026, before approving a

form of notice of this proceeding to EPE’s customers and before approving a method for

disseminating that form of notice.



                                      Respectfully submitted,
